Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Procurement asked me to circle back on a couple of items in the draft order form before we run this to legal on our side:

1) Invoice routing: CloudScale prefers invoices sent to finance@cloudscale.com and we need a legal entity mapping in the order form so our AP knows which entity to pay. Can Redwood confirm the remit-to entity on the invoice and whether you can send a separate invoice per-entity if we split the commitment?

2) Escrow / prepay trigger: We have a standard practice where any prepaid credit > $250k must be placed in escrow or held on our side with a two-stage release. Is there a fallback language you can accept for prepay credits (we're OK with a credit ledger but need clear release events tied to usage)?

3) Net terms: We typically ask for net 45 for enterprise pilots. What are Redwood's standard terms for dedicated/reserved commitments? Any flexibility?

Also flagging VAT/responsibility — if a CloudScale EU entity is the payer we will need to apply reverse-charge per local guidance; please confirm whether Redwood will accept a reverse-charge flow or if you require VAT to be charged on the invoice.

Appreciate quick confirmation so we can move to the purchase order.

Best,
Maya Singh

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below.

• Invoice routing / remit entity: Redwood can issue invoices to the Redwood US entity by default. We can also provide separate invoices per Redwood entity if the order is explicitly split by legal entity in the order form. If CloudScale provides the PO with the target paying entity, we will route accordingly.

• Escrow / prepay: We do not typically use third-party escrow for hosted credits. Two pragmatic options we can offer:
  1) Prepay credit held as a segregated customer credit on our balance sheet with explicit release events (usage drawdown or 12-month expiration), or
  2) Escrow-style holdback (only for > $250k) with release tied to monthly usage reports.

I attached a draft order form (OrderForm_Draft_v3.pdf) and a redline reflecting option (1) language. Ben and Karthik — please review the suggested escrow fallback and the net terms language below.

• Net terms: Our standard for order-forms with reserved capacity is net 30. For enterprise pilots or large deals we can move to net 45 with a signed SOW or an approved finance exception (executed by Finance and Sales leadership). If CloudScale is ready to commit to minimums for the pilot period, we can accept net 45.

Action items:
- Ben: provide final redline for the "prepay credit" clause to make it legal-ready.
- Karthik: confirm handling for VAT reverse-charge and whether we need to add a clause for VAT evidence (certificate of business status).
- Maya: send PO/pdf with target paying entity and any required invoice fields.

Thanks — attaching both files for reference.

Best,

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: Prepaid credit and escrow fallback
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.inference>

Suggested clause (excerpt):
"Prepaid Credits. Customer may prepay for Services. Prepaid amounts will be held as a segregated customer credit on Vendor's balance sheet and applied against future usage. For any Prepaid Credit amount in excess of USD 250,000, upon Customer's written request, the parties agree to utilize an independent escrow or trust mechanism reasonably acceptable to both parties, with release events tied to either (i) documented monthly usage statements or (ii) the expiration of the credit term (12 months), whichever occurs first. In the absence of a Customer request for escrow, Vendor shall maintain a customer credit ledger and provide monthly usage reports upon request."
Net terms: "Unless otherwise agreed in a Finance Exception, invoices are due within thirty (30) days from the date of invoice. For Customers with an executed finance exception (documented in the Order Form), payment terms may be extended to forty-five (45) days)."

VAT: recommending explicit line: "Taxes and VAT. Unless otherwise required by law, Customer is responsible for VAT, sales or similar taxes. If Customer provides valid reverse-charge evidence and the underlying transaction qualifies for reverse charge under applicable law, Vendor will not charge VAT and Customer will self-account for VAT in its jurisdiction. Vendor may request documentation (VAT registration number or certificate) prior to issuing a reverse-charge invoice."

This should cover the major asks. Karthik — if you agree on reverse-charge verification (certificate + VAT reg number) we can add a short checklist to the order form so AP doesn't block payment.

Ben
General Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference
